title: Talk with Us, Lord, Thyself Reveal
description: Talk with Us, Lord, Thyself Reveal in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 503 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Seeking God”, where the book credits them to the Methodist Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Talk with us, Lord, thy-self re-veal, While here o'er earth we rove; Speak to our hearts, and let us feel The kin-dling of thy love.

lines: Talk with us, Lord, thyself reveal,
While here o'er earth we rove;
Speak to our hearts, and let us feel
All time, and toil, and care;
Labor is rest, and pain is sweet,
If thou, my God, art here.
Here, then, my God, vouchsafe to stay,
My bounding heart shall own thy sway,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
